title: Launch Sprint Ops Slate — compact calendar & preflight checklist (May 2026)
body:
Purpose:
This is a compact, pragmatic operations slate intended to be used by the release engineer and on-call SRE during a short launch sprint. It combines a tight timeboxed rollout calendar (48–72h window), a prioritized preflight checklist, a lightweight role matrix, and an annotated release-notes draft that can be copy/pasted into the product docs.

Scope and assumptions:
- Scope: rollout of hosted-api v2.14.0 (performance improvements, small schema change for diagnostics header, routing policy update). No database migrations.
- Target deployment window: 2026-05-15 08:00 UTC → 2026-05-17 08:00 UTC (48h active period, 72h monitoring guardrails).
- Assumptions: Canary capacity available, Dedicated pools unaffected, Private deployments unaffected by control plane changes.

Quick role matrix (who does what):
- Release Lead: Aisha Patel — overall coordination, go/no-go decisions, stakeholder comms.
- SRE Runbook Owner: Liam Chen — execute infra steps, monitor metrics, trigger rollback if SLO breach.
- Release Engineer: Sofia Martinez — manage model bundles, orchestrate canary, watch deploy pipeline.
- QA & Post-verification Lead: Priya Nair — run smoke tests, regression prompts, accept post-release verification.
- Communication Liaison: Diego Alvarez — updates to #release-coord, customer success alerting if needed.

Compact rollout calendar (timeboxed):
- T-minus 72h (2026-05-12): Finalize release notes draft, tag release branch, confirm canary capacity. Owners: Release Lead + Release Engineer.
- T-minus 48h (2026-05-13): Freeze feature flags for the release, ensure all merged PRs are green, run release smoke locally. Owner: Release Engineer.
- T-minus 24h (2026-05-14): Preflight runbook dry-run: full checklist (below). SRE run executes preflight scripts in staging mirror. Owner: SRE Runbook Owner.
- T-minus 2h (2026-05-15 06:00 UTC): Standup — 20m. Confirm metrics dashboards, alert thresholds, rollback window. Owner: Release Lead.
- T0 (2026-05-15 08:00 UTC): Push canary lanes (5% traffic) across two regions (us-west1, eu-west1). Owner: Release Engineer.
- T0 + 15m: Basic health check — 5m: latency P50/P95 within baseline, errors < 0.1%. Owner: SRE.
- T0 + 2h: If healthy, increase canary to 20% across all canary pools. Owner: Release Engineer.
- T0 + 6h: Full rollout to hosted-api (gradual ramp to 100% over 3 hours) if no signal degradation. Owner: Release Lead decision.
- T+48h: End of active rollout window. Begin extended verification (observability checks, regression prompts). Owner: QA Lead.
- T+72h: Release declared stable or rollback completed. Release notes finalized and published. Owner: Release Lead.

Preflight checklist (must pass before T0):
- [ ] Release branch created and tagged: v2.14.0. (PR: #1392)
- [ ] All merge-blocking CI green for release branch. (CI: build, unit, integration, smoke)
- [ ] Canary capacity reserved and verified in us-west1 and eu-west1. (Infra ticket: INF-879)
- [ ] Rollback artifacts built and smoke-tested (previous stable tag v2.13.7).
- [ ] Monitoring dashboards prepopulated with expected baselines for tokens/sec, request latency, 5xx rate, queue depth.
- [ ] Alert thresholds reviewed and two-tier actions documented (automated autoscale, manual rollback).
- [ ] Runbook snippets for common failure modes accessible in runbooks repo, link copied to #release-coord.
- [ ] Security scan completed for new diagnostic header flag. No high/critical findings.
- [ ] Customer-impacting changes flagged and comms draft prepared for CS & account teams.
- [ ] Post-release verification set (prompt-regression suite, sampling scripts) and owners assigned.

Rollout decision tree (simplified):
- If P95 latency increases > 30% sustained over 10m -> throttle rollout, investigate kernel selection logs.
- If 5xx rate > 0.5% for 5m or errors from model runtime spike -> immediate rollback to v2.13.7 and open incident.
- If memory pressure on GPU nodes > 85% -> scale down rollout and enable emergency autoscale policy.

Rollback plan (fast path):
- Trigger rollback job: infra/rollback-to-stable.yml (an automated job that replaces model variant and restarts serving tasks).
- Communicate in #release-coord: "Rollback initiated — rolling to v2.13.7 for hosted-api. Incident created: INC-RELEASE-599".
- Notify CS/SEs with affected customers list (if any).
- Post-rollback verification: smoke suite run + 30m observation window.

Observability checklist (what to watch):
- Key dashboards: tokens-per-second, per-route latency (P50/P95/P99), 5xx ratio, model-kv-cache-hit-rate, avg-batch-size, GPU memory usage.
- Logs to tail: runtime.stderr (model), router.info (routing decisions), kernel-selector.info (compilation warnings).
- Synthetic checks: run 200 prompt samples through streaming interface; compare output length and basic correctness heuristics.
- Error digests: sample first 100 unique traces for triage.

Smoke commands (operational snippets):
- Kick off canary (internal script): ./scripts/deploy_canary --tag v2.14.0 --regions us-west1,eu-west1 --weight 5
- Rollback quick: ./scripts/rollback --to-tag v2.13.7 --target hosted-api
- Run regression prompts: python tools/prompt_regression.py --suite release_smoke_2026_may --sample 200

Post-release verification (first 48h):
- QA: run regression suite at T+6h, T+24h, T+48h. Log results in linked artifacts.
- SRE: confirm no SEV-level alerts, CPU/GPU no anomalies, autoscale behaved as expected.
- Product: validate diagnostic header feature in 10 real requests across regions.
- CS: monitor critical customer telemetry for any sustained deviations; be ready to open customer tickets.

Lightweight annotated release notes (DRAFT — copy to product-release-notes on signoff):
Release v2.14.0 (DRAFT) — May 2026
Highlights:
- Improved serving kernel selection heuristics for medium-length sequences, reducing P95 latency by ~10% on average for common prompt shapes.
- New diagnostics header: adds X-RW-Req-Debug to responses when enabled (opt-in). Useful for tracing request routing and kernel selection.
- Routing policy update: prefer lower-cost model variants when latency budget >= 120ms to reduce per-token cost.

Technical notes for operators:
- No database migrations. Backwards-compatible diagnostic header; disabled by default for customers.
- If you see increased compilation warnings in kernel-selector.info, consider increasing compilation cache size or pinning kernel versions for affected nodes.

Known issues:
- Small subset of prompts with long context (>4096 tokens) may trigger increased memory churn; we have mitigations in the autoscale policy but not a complete fix.
- Function-calling payloads with deeply nested JSON sometimes increased per-request CPU in our tests; monitoring is enabled.

Open questions / TODOs (need answers before finalizing notes):
- [ ] Confirm if diagnostic header should be documented in public API reference or remain in internal docs behind feature flag. (Owner: Product)
- [ ] Decide if we want a soft-launch email to top 20 customers or wait until T+72h. (Owner: CS)

Appendix: quick links and runbook IDs
- Full runbook: confluence:Runbooks/Hosted-API-Release-Flow
- Rollback job: github.com/redwood-inference/infra/.github/workflows/rollback.yml
- Canary capacity ticket: INF-879
- Incident template: confluence:Incidents/SEV-Template

Notes to self (rough):
- Keep canary small and regional — previous deploys showed transient regional latency spikes when we ramped too quickly.
- If memory churn occurs, prefer to reduce batch cap rather than increase node count as temporary mitigation; reduces tail latency variation.
- Save metric snapshots before T0 and at each ramp step (scripts/metrics_snapshot.sh).

Immediate next steps (today):
- Finalize the release notes draft with Product and CS (by 2026-05-06). (Owner: Release Lead)
- Confirm canary capacity reservations and run dry-run in staging mirror (by 2026-05-10). (Owner: SRE)
- Post preflight dry-run results in #release-coord no later than 2026-05-14 18:00 UTC. (Owner: Release Engineer)

End of slate. Keep edits minimal in last 24h before rollout; use comments in doc for minor clarifications.
